item.title: In 'Ply,' Hernán Díaz imagines what we become after the world we know
item.description: Pulitzer prize winner Hernán Díaz' new book 'Ply' follows a young woman who siphons electricity to power punk shows in a re-wilded world. Díaz tells NPR how the novel came to examine selfhood, identity and intimacy.

item.title: Supreme Court starts a new term with a case about who pays for climate damage
item.description: The Supreme Court starts its new term with a Colorado county's claim that an oil refinery worsened climate change. The ruling could determine whether similar cases can move forward.

item.title: How much are AI data centers adding to your electricity bill?
item.description: Americans are worried AI data centers will raise their electricity bills. Congress has come up with a plan to protect ratepayers, but there's no easy way to find out what AI is costing them.

item.description: Trump said Clayton will lead the White House's new "Super Intelligence Force," which will coordinate government engagement with artificial intelligence.

item.title: How the Cornell case is affecting women who have experienced sexual assault
item.description: The rape allegations that have emerged from a Cornell University frat house are leading many women to remember their own experiences — and call for a wider reckoning over sexual violence.

item.title: Families of journalists killed in Ukraine sue Fox News for failing to keep them safe
item.description: Fox News is being sued by families of two journalists killed in Ukraine four years ago. They say the network failed to keep their loved ones safe.

item.title: Do fraternities fuel sexual assaults on campus?
item.description: Fraternities are at the center of recent debate over sexual assault on campus. Studies show Greek life is linked to higher rates of sexual assault, but researchers say it's a broader systemic problem.

item.title: Latter-day Saints women turn away from scandal-plagued Republican candidate in Arizona
item.description: Arizona Republican candidate for Congress Mark Lamb has been accused of sexual misconduct while sheriff. His controversy is turning many voters away as Democrats see an opportunity in the red seat.
